description: Verify that DUT implements Nagle: with outstanding unacknowledged data, additional small writes are buffered until the prior segment is acked (RFC 1122 §4.2.3.4)
approach:
[Objective]
Nagle's algorithm coalesces small writes to reduce header overhead. RFC 1122 §4.2.3.4: when there is unacked data outstanding, additional small writes wait for the prior segment's ACK.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester ⇄ DUT: handshake.
2. DUT (UT) sends small write #1 → DUT → Tester: data #1.
3. DUT (UT) sends small write #2 → DUT must NOT emit immediately (data #1 unacked).
4. Tester → DUT: ACK of data #1.
5. Observation: DUT → Tester: data #2 (now released).

[Pass condition]
Data #2 emitted only AFTER ACK of data #1.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_first_data — DUT did not emit first segment
• Fail_dut_sent_second_segment_before_ack — Nagle violation
• Fail_no_second_data — DUT never released second segment

verdicts.Fail_dut_sent_second_segment_before_ack: DUT sent second segment before ACK (Nagle violation)
verdicts.Fail_no_second_data: No DUT second data segment after ACK
